Do not invent unsupported news or why-choose-us sections because they are not present in the provided contentMap.

heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro—advanced foundation models for professional visual content creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a high-impact split narrative inside a dark, full-bleed hero: left side carries the headline, short proof line, and orange CTA; right side uses a layered product collage with floating UI shells, output frames, and a silent autoplay video preview card for Seedance. Avoid a generic image-right treatment by offsetting the media stack upward and overlapping it with a secondary gallery strip below. Add a subtle grid overlay and orange orb highlights to reinforce the operational-dashboard premium feel. Keep the hero media-first, enterprise-clean, and dramatic, with orange as the only action color.

repetitionBreakers: Dark split hero with media collage
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro by ByteDance | AI Image and Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore ByteDance’s Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro for professional AI image and video generation. Create high-resolution visuals, cinematic video, and synchronized audio with enterprise-grade control.

sections.backgroundTreatment: dark charcoal base with floating output frames, prompt chips, waveform accents, and orange highlight glows
sections.designNote: Make the hero text-first but visually dynamic: headline answers what this is, subheadline names professionals and teams, and the CTA is the only visible action. Right side shows layered image and video outputs to signal both Seedream and Seedance immediately. Keep supporting copy compact so the ad-message continuity is obvious.

Place trust early because traffic is warm and proof type is logos. Use a strong logo marquee with 3-6 recognizable creative and enterprise brands; if logo count is limited, fall back to a metric strip. Keep it high-contrast and compact so it reads as authority, not decoration.

Split into two alternating product blocks with distinct visual energy. First block: Seedream 4.5 as a spotlight section with a preview panel and a compact grid of the strongest 4-5 capabilities, emphasizing text-image alignment, resolution, typographic rendering, and composition control. Second block: Seedance 1.5 Pro in a darker or inverted panel with video-first gallery cards, audio waveform cues, and a more cinematic preview to differentiate it. Because both sections have 5+ features, use spotlight-plus-grid instead of a flat list.

Use a testimonial carousel because there are 4+ quotes. Focus on role-led credibility from creative director, video producer, art director, and marketing manager. Keep the presentation sparse and premium, with one quote enlarged at a time and subtle metadata beneath.

Do not turn pricing into a comparison table. Present two centered cards with one clear commercial path per product, using the same CTA label: Get started. Emphasize the value story and keep the card hierarchy simple, since the page is about high-trust lead conversion rather than ecommerce browsing.

Use the final conversion section as a dark, high-contrast close with a floating card. Keep the CTA full-width on mobile and use only the allowed CTA label Get started. The form should feel like a next-step action after proof and product clarity, not an interruption.

Reserve the final thin strip for secondary credibility or compliance-style logo repetition only if needed. Keep it visually lighter than the main trust bar so the page ends with conversion energy, not redundant proof.

blueprint.designPersonality: A premium, media-first AI platform page with enterprise confidence, strong logo-led trust, and a dark orange-accent system that feels like a high-end content production dashboard rather than a generic SaaS landing page.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a premium media-collage approach: a dark hero visual with floating output frames, UI shells, prompt chips, and a prominent video gallery strip. Trust logos should dominate the proof area with a marquee band of recognizable enterprise and creative logos in SVG. Use PNG for product mockups and thumbnail tiles, JPEG for the hero-wide visual atmosphere, and SVG for icons and logos. Include motion-rich gallery cards showing video outputs, audio waveform accents, and timestamp labels to reinforce Seedance 1.5 Pro.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long and needs a compact, high-clarity size to preserve hierarchy in a dark, media-rich hero.

colours.colourReason: The palette is derived exclusively from Techjockey’s brand colors: charcoal primary for the dark hero and section anchors, orange for the CTA and highlights, white for clarity, and light grey for separation. This creates a strong product-led identity while staying brand-true.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Full-width top hero with brand/logo lockup, strong left-aligned headline block, short supporting copy, and a compact benefit list. Visual emphasis is text-first rather than image-first, with a clean marketing-banner structure.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single hero followed by a lead-capture form block, then stacked content sections with clear vertical separation. The page favors long-scroll, linear persuasion flow over dense multi-column layouts.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple rectangular content blocks with light borders or subtle elevation, minimal ornamentation, and utility-driven spacing. Cards are likely used for form and content grouping rather than decorative feature tiles.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA is prominent and action-oriented in the hero, with secondary conversion handled through a dedicated form section. CTA hierarchy is simple: one main action per section, with supporting form submit as the main conversion path.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing module is visually present in the reference structure; if added, it should follow the same low-friction lead-gen pattern rather than a comparison-table heavy ecommerce layout.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not visible in the provided reference markup; likely a standard low-profile footer with utility links and compliance elements if included.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Text-led hero with logo/brand mark and no dominant hero media. Media usage appears minimal and functional, supporting trust and recognition rather than storytelling imagery.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Stacked product/feature sections with bold section labels, large headlines, concise explanatory copy, and bullet-like feature lists. The structure supports progressive disclosure: overview first, then capability breakdown.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form card placed immediately after the hero, visually separated from the banner. Form pattern is conversion-first, with hidden tracking fields and a compact, focused field layout.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static marketing page with no evident motion system in the provided structure; interaction design should remain restrained and utility-led.
designNotes: Use a clean enterprise B2B visual language with clear hierarchy and minimal decoration.
Keep the page linear and conversion-focused, reducing cognitive load through short sections and repeated CTA opportunities.
Prefer large typography, generous whitespace, and simple list-based feature communication.
Separate brand messaging from lead capture with a distinct form panel.
Avoid carousel-heavy or interaction-heavy patterns unless additional content demands them.

blueprint.additionalInstructions:
PROOF STRATEGY: The visitor trusts logos most. Make this the dominant trust signal.

use dark theme and a gallery section containing videos

mustHaveMoments: Dark-theme hero with a sharp value proposition for both image and video generation
Prominent logo-led trust strip immediately below the hero
Product explanation blocks for Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro with clear separation
Video gallery section showcasing generated outputs and motion quality
Use-case-driven proof section for creative, marketing, and production teams
Pricing or quote cards framed as consultation-led conversion, not ecommerce
Testimonial section with role-based credibility from creative professionals
Persistent primary CTA repeated across sections
avoidPatterns: Light or playful visual treatment that reduces enterprise credibility
Image-first hero that competes with the message
Dense comparison tables or overly technical architecture diagrams
Badge-only trust without visible brand/logo validation
Overly decorative cards, gradients, or gimmicky motion effects
Too many competing CTAs in the same viewport
Long paragraphs without scannable feature hierarchy
designStrategy.reasoning: This page should convert solution-aware professionals who are evaluating advanced generative AI for production use, so the strategy should be lead-gen focused with a strong demo/quote pathway. Because the visitor trusts logos most, trust must be anchored by a prominent logo strip and brand validation rather than testimonials or badges alone. The product is technically sophisticated and benefits from a product-led narrative that clearly separates Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro while still presenting them as a unified ByteDance visual content stack. A dark theme supports the premium, futuristic positioning and helps video/gallery content stand out. The hero should be split and message-led to preserve clarity while allowing room for immediate CTA and trust reinforcement. Gallery videos are essential because motion output is a key differentiator for Seedance, but the layout should remain balanced and not feel like a media showcase detached from conversion.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
